added_lines: Our business activities are shaped by an increasingly complex environment and ever new risk potentials. Digitalisation is changing our customers’ expectations while at the same time opening up new ways of reaching them. The impacts of climate change are also challenging us. They are already having a noticeable effect on our business today.

We view economic prosperity, resilience and technological progress as building blocks of a fairer, more sustainable society and act responsibly and with foresight over the long term. As part of the Munich Re Group, ERGO is guided by a shared sustainability strategy. As a responsible corporate Group, Munich Re endeavours to play its part in meeting the goals of the Paris Agreement with its Climate Ambition 2030. Munich Re expresses this intention in the expectation that governments will meet their own pledges, in order to ensure that the goals of the Paris Agreement are achieved.

Along the value chain, we take social, environmental and economic criteria – so called ESG criteria – into account beyond climate change. These include protecting human rights and biodiversity, as well as supporting international conventions on controversial weapons, which we have anchored in our investment and insurance guidelines.

In the long term, Munich Re remains committed to reducing greenhouse gas emissions across its entire (re)insurance business and investment portfolio to net zero* by 2050, thereby contributing to the achievement of the Paris Agreement’s targets. Munich Re has set out its targets for 2030 and its long-term intentions for 2040 and 2050 on the assumption that governments will honour their own commitments to achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement.

With these targets, Munich Re consistently continues along the path defined in the Climate Ambition 2025 of the Munich Re Group Ambition 2025, which applied up to and including the 2025 financial year and was successfully implemented.
An overview and definition of the targets and intentions of the Munich Re Group Climate Ambition 2030 can be found
. The ERGO Group contributes to the targets of the Munich Re Group Climate Ambition.

* With regard to the definition and scope of net zero, as well as how it can be achieved, we will take into account applicable regulations, industry best practice, offsetting requirements and climate research when setting our next climate ambition(s). Further interim targets and measures required beyond the stated 2030 targets to achieve the long-term goal for 2050 will be set out in the next climate ambition(s).
Mitigate risks. Allocate capital. Shape the future.
Our core business is taking on and diversifying risk. Our business conduct is driven by appropriate risk management and an approach that combines economic success with social responsibility.

In our insurance business, we achieve this in particular through strong customer focus, responsible solutions and the integration of ESG aspects into our products and services. Munich Re’s approach with regard to the climate is based on three core elements:
provision of risk-transfer solutions that contribute to climate change adaptation and to mitigating the impacts of climate change

ERGO contributes to the Group wide climate strategy, with the long term aim of reducing GHG emissions associated with its primary insurance business to net zero* by 2050. Our decarbonisation targets focus in particular on specific activities in connection with thermal coal and oil and gas production. Intermediate targets have been set for 2030, together with concrete measures that are specified in the

We support the adaptation of society and the economy to climate change by offering insurance solutions that help our customers to obtain financial protection against natural catastrophes and extreme weather events. Insurance solutions against natural catastrophe losses in various lines of business – such as homeowners, household contents, motor, and commercial and industrial insurance – contribute to this.

To ensure that ESG aspects are taken into account in the insurance business, ERGO applies the Group wide ESG criteria, processes, tools and underwriting guidelines. Climate and ESG experts, as well as dedicated sustainability teams, support the business units in integrating these aspects into underwriting.

As a global investor, we are aware of our responsibility to conduct our activities sustainably and integrate sustainability criteria into our investment policy. The Munich Re Group – and thus also ERGO – aims to steer the GHG emissions of its investment portfolio towards net zero by 2050. To ensure transparency and accountability on our path to net zero, specific climate targets have been defined for the various asset classes by 2030, including decarbonisation targets, climate tackling investments and engagement targets (for details, please refer to
The measures initiated to achieve these targets are essentially based on the decarbonisation lever of portfolio reallocation. This includes, among other things, the use of CO

e budgets for specific portfolios and divestments, as well as investments in low carbon assets. At the same time, we restrict or exclude direct investments in listed companies (equities and corporate bonds) that generate material revenues from thermal coal or oil sands, have material annual production of or power generation capacity from thermal coal, or are classified as specialised or integrated types of oil and gas companies. In addition, selected companies – identified through a structured process – are encouraged and supported in developing and implementing their climate ambitions and climate approaches as part of so called engagement dialogues.

provides the framework for taking sustainability criteria into account in our investments. It also sets out which direct investments are excluded. These include, among other things, investments in companies that manufacture controversial weapons (such as biological weapons and cluster munitions), as well as trading and related derivatives in food related commodities such as grains/oilseeds or dairy products. To address human rights violations with appropriate measures, we also exclude states and companies with significant breaches from our direct investments. To limit negative impacts on areas of protected biodiversity, we are guided by the lists of World Heritage properties relating to natural sites and mixed natural and cultural properties maintained under the UNESCO World Heritage Convention. Special review processes apply to investments in affected areas.

For the systematic selection of investments based on sustainability criteria, we rely, among other things, on data from leading providers of sustainability analyses and ratings. The majority of the Group’s investments are managed by the Group’s own asset manager MEAG.
Customer dialogue and customer satisfaction at ERGO

ERGO’s success largely depends on maintaining a close and trusting relationship with our customers. That is why we aim to understand their needs and develop appropriate solutions together in dialogue – across all channels and along the entire customer relationship.
Feedback as the foundation for continuous improvement

Responsibility for customer satisfaction lies with the respective Boards of Management and managing directors of the ERGO companies in the various countries. To systematically manage customer satisfaction, regular independent customer surveys are conducted in primary insurance in key core markets via market research panels and ERGO wide centralised platforms. The aim is to obtain a market view that is as neutral as possible from the customer’s perspective. The results show how satisfied customers are with ERGO compared with competitors and where there is potential for improvement or differentiation. These insights feed into the further development of our products, services and processes. In addition to customer feedback, customer complaints are also recorded and evaluated. The responses are used as a basis for improvements in the various areas.
Digital transformation for better customer experiences

ERGO is driving its own transformation into a digitally leading insurer in Germany and its international core markets. Along the entire value chain – from products and processes through to services – digital technologies are deployed in a targeted way. These include, among others, key technologies such as artificial intelligence, voice robotics, virtual reality and process mining. In addition, ERGO makes use of strategic partnerships with global technology companies as well as start ups and scale ups. The aim is to make processes faster and more efficient and to offer digital solutions that facilitate access to insurance products, simplify communication and enable faster feedback.
Read our //radar magazine to find out what is currently moving us in the area of sustainability and commitment.
Climate strategy and reporting within the Munich Re Group

Our parent company Munich Re provides detailed reporting on the implementation of climate targets in the insurance business and in investments, as well as on measures to enhance customer focus and customer satisfaction, in its Group Annual Report.

Responsible business practices

In our business, the environment we work in is becoming ever more complex and new risks are arising all the time. Digitalisation changes customer’s expectations and at the same time opens up new ways to approach them. We also face the challenges posed by climate change which already have a tangible impact on our business.

ERGO is ready to meet the challenges of this changing landscape. Our customers and their needs are at the centre of all we do. We will continue to expand our range of products and services that are easily available via digital channels. In addition to our insurance solutions and products taking into account environmental protection, we also provide customers with investment options related to sustainability for their wealth management.

Clarity and innovation for the best solutions
At the heart of all we do - Our customers

Our customers’ needs and requirements govern all we do as a business. We demonstrate our customer orientation with clear communication, easy-to-understand and easily accessible products, a wide range of opportunities for customers to give us their feedback, and top-quality customer advice.
Clear communication: comprehensible contract documents

We use clear language to ensure our customers know exactly what we are offering them, and give them descriptive and comprehensible information rather than losing ourselves in complex specialist terms. We adhere to clear-language criteria certified by external experts, and substantially revised our contract documents and product information. External auditors accompanied this process over several years and regularly reviewed the comprehensibility of our customer communication.
Feedback counts: Customer Workshop

We engage our customers in dialogue, and they reward us with their feedback and new ideas. Customers who join the ERGO Customer Workshop have the opportunity to support and shape ERGO with their constructive criticism and their suggestions. Customers can also submit their feedback online at any time – we’re always open to suggestions and keen to improve our service.
Voice intelligence: taking out insurance via a voice dialog
For the convenient completion of insurance policies, ERGO also relies on voice intelligence. For example, customers can purchase travel health insurance entirely through a voice dialogue.
Focus on environmental protection, technology and customer needs
Forward-thinking solutions

For ERGO, sustainability is also reflected in insurance solutions. When we develop new products, doing justice to changing customer needs and protecting the environment come high up on our priority list, as well as accompanying new technological developments.
ESG criteria: an integral part of product development

The consideration of ethical, social and governance aspects – in short: ESG aspects - is firmly incorporated in our product development process. We also live up to our corporate responsibility with our responsible underwriting policy. In particular, we want to contribute to mitigating the impact of climate change and support the transition to renewable energies with our products. Our
Group
consequently took the decision to not insure any new coal-fired power plants or coal mines.
Supporting the energy transition and climate protection

ERGO provides a broad spectrum of insurance products and services which take environmental issues into account. Other insurance solutions address social challenges. For example, microinsurance products, modelled on the microcredit principle, are becoming ever more popular in developing and emerging nations such as India. They help to secure livelihoods, e.g. following earthquakes or floods.

Microinsurance in India

Microinsurance has come a long way in recent years, helping to improve the lives of many millions of people around the world. Our India-based joint venture HDFC ERGO, which has been developing and selling insurance products for rural contexts since 2008, offers a diverse range of microinsurance solutions such as health, accident, fire insurance or specific cover for livestock and equipment essential to people’s livelihoods.
Access to insurance in emerging markets such as India

ERGO uses special solutions to contribute to building up insurance markets in developing countries and emerging economies with the focus on long-term growth perspectives. One example of such a market is India, where the overwhelming majority of the population has no access to traditional insurance products. Our German-Indian joint-venture company HDFC ERGO develops microinsurance policies in close cooperation with non-governmental organisations and microfinance institutes. The key factor for the products is that they must have a transparent structure, need to be marketed at an affordable rate, and can be sold through innovative sales channels.
Diversity in microinsurance
The policies range from health insurance, through accident and property cover, to protection against the loss of working animals, and failed harvests.
Innovation in weather insurance for crop failures

On behalf of the Indian government, HDFC ERGO was the first private insurance company to launch a weather insurance policy for failed harvests on the market in 2010. The structure of this product is simple and a flat-rate payment is made to reduce the financial risks of failed harvests if a specified temperature or level of precipitation is exceeded or not achieved.
Insurance policies with environmental features

ERGO supports ecology-minded customers by extending its care for the environment into its product range. Our portfolio ranges from insurance cover for renewable energies and eco-rates for car insurance to unit-linked annuity insurance which also take environmental issues into account if desired.

The finite nature of fossil fuels and ever stricter environmental and climate protection standards have given renewable energies a role of key significance in today’s world. ERGO is supplying its expertise to help support technological developments in this field, providing the insurance cover which is vital to the use of these forward-looking sources of energy.

Environmental protection and scarce resources demand a new way of thinking about our traditional energy supply. We support the establishment of renewable energy sources using customised insurance solutions.
Insurance solutions for a sustainable energy supply

Renewable energies and relevant technologies have steadily gained in importance during the past years - not only in the eyes of consumers, but for companies as well. Corporate customers in Germany can purchase our combined property and business interruption insurance providing extensive cover for photovoltaic systems. Our homeowners’ insurance covers claims under the insured perils – for example fire or storm – to photovoltaic, solar and heat-pump systems used for private purposes.
Protection for photovoltaic systems with reduced yield insurance

The photovoltaics market is an area of particular focus for us. ERGO is one of the few insurers to offer an innovative form of extended cover for reduced yields, which covers losses incurred when the energy produced by the system in a year falls short of expectations due to causes such as low levels of solar radiation or faults with components in the system.
Protecting ecological systems

European environmental legislation increasingly requires polluters of flora and fauna, bodies of water or soil to take responsibility for their actions. In case of damage, high reconstruction costs could pose an existential threat for customer’s business. In Germany, ERGO helps customers meet this risk by offering liability cover for environmental damage. Since 2009, cover for environmental damage has become a fixed part of our corporate liability insurance policies.
Handling capital with care
Our investments

Sustainability criteria also apply to investments made for the ERGO Group. We take account of our responsibility by prudent and far-sighted investment management supported by a sophisticated controlling system.
Maximum security for customers

Investment guidelines drawn up by our parent company Munich Re and the Principles for Responsible Investments (PRI) which we signed up to in 2006, provide the framework for our sustainable investment strategy across the Group.

The primary objective of our investment management is to be in a position to meet our commitments to customers at all times. The following objective applies to all lines of business: maximum security for the investors. The investment strategies are based on the differing insurance benefits. For example, in a traditional life insurance the guaranteed benefits must be generated alongside the bonus, whereas health insurance demands the ability to pay ongoing costs and making provision to pay for any higher health benefits as customers get older. We therefore need to ensure in all lines that the maturities for our investments match the terms for our commitments.
Managing commitments strategically

As a global investor, we are conscious of our responsibility to act sustainably and therefore integrate ESG criteria into our investment policy. Munich Re has set itself the goal of moving its portfolio towards a net-zero climate target by the year 2050. In that context, we have committed to divesting from thermal coal by 2040. Already today, we no longer invest in companies that generate more than 30 percent of their earnings from thermal coal mining or power generation from coal.

The Responsible Investment Guideline provides the framework for our investment management. It also sets out which topic areas cannot be considered for direct investment. These include, amongst other things, in-vestments in producers of controversial weapons (such as anti-personnel mines or cluster munition), as well as trading in or investments in food-related commodities (such as grain, oil seeds or dairy products). To combat human rights violations, we also exclude from our direct investments states and companies that are guilty of serious violations.

To ensure that investments are selected systematically based on ESG criteria, we rely, amongst other things, on data from leading providers of sustainability analyses and ratings. The bulk of the Group’s investments are managed by the Group’s asset manager MEAG.
